extensions.note: Values are read from Kotlin/Compose source (Theme.kt, Water.kt, Charts.kt, Components.kt, Nav.kt, screens/Common.kt). The build compiles but has never been rendered on a device; HTML/CSS in the components array is a web approximation for panel preview only and is not the shipped implementation.

money-hero.purpose: Safe-to-spend over the water surface on Home. At most one per screen.

money-large.purpose: A screen's headline figure inside a plate.

money-row.purpose: Every ledger amount; the tabular column that aligns on the decimal.

headline-small.purpose: SectionHeading title. No eyebrow above it.

label-medium.purpose: Captions above figures, and flag text.

shadows.name: none
shadows.purpose: The system ships no shadows. Elevation is a depth argument that picks a bed tint and alpha.

shadows.name: specular-edge
shadows.value: 1.2dp stroke, horizontal gradient transparent -> #3DBFE0FF -> transparent, across a 22dp top-corner arc
shadows.purpose: The only stroke on a plate. Top edge only; loses 25% alpha per depth step.

depthLadder.purpose: At the surface. The default plate.
Under the page's emphasis: empty states, secondary blocks.
A plate nested inside another plate.
The floor. Also the bed of every gauge, vessel and water column.

motion.name: water-level
motion.purpose: The one authored motion: the Home water column's level rise.

motion.name: swell
motion.purpose: Two summed sine waves on the water surface. Home hero only.

motion.name: caustic-drift
motion.purpose: The ground's three scatters. Runs only on Home and Lock.

motion.name: chart-reveal
motion.purpose: Ring sweep, vessel fill, sounding-line reveal.

motion.name: detail-push
motion.value: slideInHorizontally 280ms at width/5 + fadeIn 200ms; pop slideOut 260ms + fadeOut 160ms
motion.purpose: Into and out of a detail screen.

motion.name: motion-gate
motion.purpose: Every animated surface reads this first and collapses to a zero-duration tween when off.

breakpoints.name: compact
breakpoints.purpose: Bottom navigation bar, five equal destinations.

breakpoints.name: expanded
breakpoints.purpose: Navigation rail on the leading edge.

categoryScale.note: Eight steps, no warm hue. #F6C566 is excluded on purpose.

narrative.overview:
The screen is a column of water lit from above. Depth, not shadow, is the only elevation mechanism: a surface nearer the top of the stack is lighter and more translucent because it is nearer the light, and a surface buried under others is denser navy. Material 3's tonal elevation already works this way, so the metaphor rides the platform instead of fighting it.

The system's thesis is that the figure and the field are the same fact. Safe-to-spend is set at 54sp over a water surface whose fill height IS that figure; remaining days run down the right edge as a gauge of ticks. The app refuses the fintech dashboard header - balance plus a row of stat chips - and it refuses a card inset on four sides for the one thing the user opened the app to read. Plates transmit rather than refract: their beds are translucent so the ground's gradient and its slow caustics read through every card. There is no backdrop blur anywhere in the build, by decision - Compose at this version has no backdrop filter, and a fake blur would be the dishonest half of the material.

Density is calm and list-led. One warm hue exists in the whole product and it is rationed. Type is Archivo throughout, run wide for money and normal for prose, tabular wherever a figure stands for real currency. The build compiles but has never been rendered on a device; every value is read from source, and claims about appearance are deliberately absent.
keyCharacteristics: Depth ladder from #17406C down to #04101D; elevation is tint and alpha, never a drop shadow.
Translucent plates lit by a 1.2dp specular hairline along the top edge only.
Archivo variable, wdth 112-118 for money, wdth 100 for text; tnum on every figure.
One warm hue (#F6C566 dark / #8A6300 light), reserved for goals and streaks.
One authored motion: the Home water column's rise and swell.

rules.name: The One Warm Hue Rule
rules.body: #F6C566 (dark) / #8A6300 (light) means goals and streaks and nothing else. It is excluded from categoryScale() on purpose, so a warm mark anywhere in the app means exactly one thing.

rules.name: The Expenses Are Not Red Rule
rules.body: Expense amounts take Expense Ink. Only over-budget and overdue reach for alert. In a tracker you log expenses all day; painting each one as an alarm makes the alarm meaningless.

rules.name: The Never-Colour-Alone Rule
rules.body: Colour never carries the direction of money by itself. Every amount has a sign and sits in a tabular column, and every over state pairs its tone with a written label - so a screen reader and a colour-blind eye get the same fact.

rules.name: The Real Money Rule
rules.body: Any figure standing for real currency is set in a MoneyType style - Archivo wide, tabular, never italic - and rendered through MoneyText. Counts, percentages and day numbers are not money and use the Material roles.

rules.name: The Cents Are Shown Rule
rules.body: Money is Long minor units formatted by moneyParts. Cents are always present and never emphasised: 64% of the base size at 52% alpha. Never Double, never rounded away.

rules.name: The No Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: A section heading carries its own weight: a title, an optional caption beneath it, and an optional trailing text action. No kicker, no numbering, no all-caps label stacked above a heading.

rules.name: The Elevation Is Depth Rule
rules.body: A plate's bed alpha and tint are a function of its depth argument and nothing else. Never a drop shadow, never a hand-picked alpha, never a border to fake a lift.

rules.name: The Transmission Rule
rules.body: Every plate lets the ground read through it. The gradient and its caustics are drawn once, behind everything; a plate that paints itself opaque buries the only reason the ground exists.

rules.name: The One Authored Motion Rule
rules.body: The Home water column's level rise (1100ms FastOutSlowInEasing) plus its 6.4s swell is the app's one authored gesture. Everything else is Material's standard grammar. Every animated surface reads motionEnabled() first and collapses to a zero-duration tween when the system's Remove animations setting is on.

rules.name: The Real FAB Rule
rules.body: One floating action per screen, and only where the primary action exists. A FAB that does nothing is worse than no FAB.

dos: Do express elevation through Plate(depth = n) / Modifier.glassPlate(shape, depth) and let the depth argument pick the bed and the edge.
Do render every currency figure through MoneyText with a MoneyType style, so it is tabular, wide, and shows cents at 64% size / 52% alpha.
Do keep money as Long minor units and format it through moneyParts.
Do reserve {colors.sun} for goals and streaks.
Do pair every over or behind-pace tone with a sign, a label, or a written sentence.
Do call motionEnabled() before any animation, and draw the ground once per shell with animate scoped to the screen that owns the hero.
Do keep the 20dp gutter, and use Modifier.bleed() when - and only when - an item is the screen's thesis.
Do leave Dynamic Color off by default and opt-in in Appearance; a wallpaper-derived scheme reorders the depth ladder until the waterline stops meaning anything.
donts: Don't add a drop shadow, an outline, or a hand-tuned alpha to fake elevation.
Don't paint an ordinary expense red.
Don't let colour be the only thing saying which way money went.
Don't put {colors.sun} into a chart scale, a category tint, or a general accent.
Don't widen ArchivoWide onto prose, or set money in the text width.
Don't round money into a Double or drop the cents.
Don't author a second hero motion, or animate the background on a screen with no hero.
Don't put a circular add button inside the navigation bar, or ship a FAB on a screen whose add-flow does not exist.
Don't stack a kicker or eyebrow above a section heading.
Don't pull in a chart library; the charts are drawn so they belong to this water.
